description: Evaluation cases for Multi-Jurisdiction (UK & India) F.I.R.E. Senior Financial Advisor skill

eval_cases.prompt: I want to spend £50,000 net per year in early retirement. How much invested wealth do I need, and why shouldn't I just use the 4% rule?
expected_criteria: Distinguishes 4% rule (30-year US horizon) from conservative UK early retirement baseline (3.25% - 3.5%)
Calculates target between £1,428,571 (at 3.5%) and £1,538,461 (at 3.25%)
Explains Lean, Standard, and Flexible/Dynamic withdrawal options
Considers future State Pension offset (~£11,500/year at age 67/68)

eval_cases.prompt: I am 34 years old with £180,000 saved. I earn £90,000, save £35,000/year, and plan to spend £42,000/year in retirement. At what age can I achieve FIRE?
expected_criteria: Calculates target portfolio (£42k / 0.035 = ~£1.2M)
Models years to FI assuming 5% real return
Projects specific retirement age (around age 47-49)
Highlights savings rate impact on the retirement timeline

eval_cases.prompt: My gross salary recently jumped to £118,000. How should I balance pension contributions, my Stocks & Shares ISA, and taxable accounts?
expected_criteria: Identifies the £100,000 - £125,140 Personal Allowance taper (the 60% tax trap, 62% with NI)
Advises salary sacrifice or SIPP contribution of £18,000 to bring adjusted net income to £100,000
Calculates immediate tax relief advantage over ISA
Explains the need to maintain sufficient ISA funding for any pre-57 early retirement bridge

eval_cases.prompt: I have £25,000 surplus cash. My mortgage is £220,000 at 5.2% with 18 years left. Should I overpay the mortgage or invest it in my ISA or Pension?
expected_criteria: Compares guaranteed tax-free return of 5.2% against expected equity returns
Explains tax relief arbitrage if client is a higher-rate (40%) taxpayer (pension relief vastly outperforms mortgage overpayment)
Evaluates the liquidity trade-off (mortgage is illiquid, ISA is accessible)
Explains how eliminating mortgage lowers living expenses and shrinks the required FIRE pot

eval_cases.prompt: I want to retire at age 46, but my private pension is locked until 57. How do I structure my bridge to fund those 11 years?
expected_criteria: Identifies the 11-year gap between retirement (46) and NMPA (57)
Calculates total bridge capital required in accessible accounts (ISAs / GIAs / Cash)
Proposes a multi-bucket architecture: Bucket 1 (1-2 yrs cash), Bucket 2 (3-5 yrs bonds/defensive), Bucket 3 (equities in ISA)
Explains the transition at 57: PCLS (25% tax-free lump sum) and basic-rate pension drawdown

eval_cases.prompt: What happens if the stock market crashes 30% right after I pull the trigger on retirement? How do I make sure I don't run out of money?
expected_criteria: Explains Sequence of Returns Risk (SORR) and the danger of selling equities at depressed prices
Outlines the 2-year cash buffer defense mechanism
Applies Guyton-Klinger capital preservation guardrail (-10% spending cut if withdrawal rate spikes >20%)
Details discretionary spending reduction and potential Barista/consulting income flex

eval_cases.prompt: I earn £130,000 and my partner earns £26,000. How do we optimize our pensions, ISAs, and assets as a couple for FIRE?
expected_criteria: Doubling allowances: £40,000 ISA allowance across two accounts
Explains danger of unequal pension pots in retirement and calculates tax savings from equalizing
Covers non-earner / lower-earner pension contribution rules (£2,880 net -> £3,600 gross)
Mentions nil gain / nil loss spousal asset transfers to utilize lower earner's CGT and basic tax band

eval_cases.prompt: I am 3 years into my FIRE plan. How should I review my progress annually, and what tells me if I am drifting off track?
expected_criteria: Outlines annual reconciliation: actual spending vs budgeted spending and portfolio CAGR vs 5% real return baseline
Defines Traffic Light framework (Green: on track / accelerate; Amber: minor drift / freeze inflation; Red: intervention / delay or cut spend)
Reviews UK tax policy updates (Budget changes to allowances, NMPA, CGT)
Rebalancing protocol between cash buffer, bonds, and equities

eval_cases.prompt: I am 32 years old living in Bengaluru with monthly expenses of ₹75,000. I have ₹25 Lakhs invested. I want to retire at 47. What is my FIRE target and monthly SIP gap?
expected_criteria: Compounds expenses at 6.5% inflation across 15 years to ~₹1.93 Lakhs/month (~₹23.15 Lakhs/year)
Applies India-calibrated SWR of 3.0% - 3.3% to calculate ~₹7.01 Crores target corpus
Projects future value of current ₹25L portfolio at 12% CAGR to ~₹1.37 Crores
Calculates monthly SIP required to bridge the remaining ₹5.65 Crores gap (~₹1.18 Lakhs/month)

eval_cases.prompt: My annual Gross Salary is ₹22 Lakhs. I pay ₹35,000/month rent in Mumbai (Metro) with Basic Salary of ₹11 Lakhs and HRA of ₹4.2 Lakhs, invest ₹1.5L in 80C, ₹50k in NPS 80CCD(1B), and ₹25k in 80D health insurance. Should I choose the Old or New Regime under the latest AY 2026-27 rules vs legacy AY 2025-26?
expected_criteria: Computes HRA exemption under the statutory 3-condition minimum formula (₹3.10 Lakhs)
Tallies eligible deductions under Old Regime (HRA + 80C + 80CCD + 80D + ₹50k standard deduction = ₹5.85 Lakhs)
Evaluates under default AY 2026-27 rules: New Regime tax is ₹2,40,500 vs Old Regime ₹3,08,880, showing New Regime saves ₹68,380 due to wide slabs and lower rates
Demonstrates versioning awareness: notes that under legacy AY 2025-26 slabs the Old Regime had saved ₹31,720, but the AY 2026-27 reforms flipped the advantage decisively to the New Regime

eval_cases.capability: India Loan Prepayment vs Equity SIP
eval_cases.prompt: I have an outstanding home loan of ₹50 Lakhs at 8.75% for 20 years. Should I prepay ₹10,000 extra per month or invest it in a Nifty 50 Index Fund SIP?
expected_criteria: Calculates reducing-balance EMI (~₹44,185/month) and total baseline interest (~₹56 Lakhs)
Calculates that paying an extra ₹10,000/month saves ~₹22.7 Lakhs in interest and cuts tenure by ~7.2 years
Compares 8.75% guaranteed risk-free return with equity after LTCG tax (12% CAGR - 12.5% tax = ~10.5% net)
Provides a balanced hybrid recommendation or clear decision criteria based on tax regime and risk tolerance

eval_cases.prompt: I earn ₹1,50,000/month, spend ₹60,000/month, pay ₹35,000 EMI, have ₹6 Lakhs in liquid funds, and want to start investing ₹50,000 in mutual funds. I don't have life insurance yet because I'm single with dependent parents. How is my financial health?
expected_criteria: Enforces Protection-First Rule: mandates pure term insurance (15x annual income = ₹2.7 Crores) before aggressive equity scaling
Evaluates Emergency Shield: 6 months of expenses + EMI = ₹5.7 Lakhs (current ₹6L is adequate)
Calculates Debt FOIR = 23.3% (healthy, < 30%)
Computes Money Health Score across the 6 dimensions and provides a prioritized action plan

eval_cases.capability: India Asset Optimization: FD, Arbitrage, Gold, Silver
eval_cases.prompt: I am in the 30% tax bracket in India. I have ₹20 Lakhs in Bank Fixed Deposits at 7.25%, and I am thinking of adding Gold and Silver. How do these assets compare after tax and inflation?
expected_criteria: Exposes the FD inflation trap: 7.25% at 31.2% tax yields 4.99% post-tax, generating -1.5% negative real return against 6.5% inflation
Recommends Arbitrage Mutual Funds as a superior tax-efficient cash parking tool (taxed at 12.5% LTCG yielding ~6.1% post-tax)
Distinguishes Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB) with 100% tax-free capital gains at RBI maturity vs Gold/Silver ETFs (12.5% LTCG after 24m)
Recommends 5%-10% Gold allocation as a currency depreciation hedge and 2%-5% max for volatile Silver

eval_cases.capability: India Real Estate: Rental Yield vs Buy vs Rent
eval_cases.prompt: I am considering buying an apartment in Bengaluru for ₹1.5 Crores (EMI ~₹1.06L/mo at 8.75%) vs renting an identical flat for ₹35,000/month and investing the rest in equity. What does the FIRE math say?
expected_criteria: Calculates gross rental yield (~2.8%) and net rental yield (~2.0% - 2.2% after maintenance, taxes, and vacancy)
Shows capital requirement disparity: generating ₹1L/month rental income requires ~₹5.5 Crores in property vs ~₹3.6 Crores in a 3.3% SWR financial portfolio
Models 20-year buy vs rent outcome showing substantial net alpha (~₹4+ Crores) in favor of renting and investing upfront capital + monthly EMI surplus into equity
Mentions post-Budget 2024 Section 112 tax rules (12.5% without indexation vs 20% grandfathered with indexation for pre-July 2024 purchases)

eval_cases.capability: India Virtual Digital Assets (Crypto) Tax & Sizing
eval_cases.prompt: I made ₹10 Lakhs profit on Bitcoin and lost ₹4 Lakhs on Ethereum this year. I want to use crypto to fund my early retirement. How much tax do I owe under Indian laws, and how should crypto fit into my FIRE plan?
expected_criteria: Enforces Section 115BBH zero loss set-off rule: explains that the ₹4L Ethereum loss CANNOT offset the ₹10L Bitcoin gain
Calculates flat 30% tax + 4% cess (31.2%) on full ₹10L gain = ₹3.12 Lakhs tax owed (52% effective tax on the ₹6L real net profit)
Highlights 1% TDS under Section 194S on sell transactions
Applies 1%-5% asymmetric satellite sizing rule; mandates that crypto must never form part of the emergency fund or core retirement floor

eval_cases.prompt: I am a higher-rate taxpayer in the UK. I realized £15,000 in crypto gains and £4,000 in crypto losses. Can I put my crypto into an ISA, and what is my tax bill?
expected_criteria: Clarifies that crypto cannot be held inside UK ISAs or standard SIPPs (held in taxable General Investment Accounts)
Calculates net capital gain: £15,000 - £4,000 = £11,000 (UK allows full loss offsetting)
Applies £3,000 annual exempt amount to arrive at £8,000 taxable gain
Computes 24% higher-rate CGT = £1,920 tax owed
Advises capping crypto at 1%-5% satellite allocation and harvesting profits into tax-sheltered ISAs

eval_cases.capability: Local Profile Storage & Private Portfolio Evaluation
eval_cases.prompt: I want to store my complete asset profile locally on my machine in a private folder ~/Documents/MyFinances/anita.json and evaluate my FIRE readiness. How does the system handle local profile storage and evaluation?
expected_criteria: Confirms 100% private local storage in the user's chosen directory with zero cloud leakage
Generates or references the unified asset profile schema covering Cash, Equities, Pensions, Precious Metals, Real Estate, Crypto, Liabilities, and Protection
Demonstrates profile-template, profile-list, and profile-eval CLI commands with custom file paths
Executes a holistic balance sheet diagnostic (liquid financial wealth, net worth, allocation %, FIRE target gap, and Money Health Score)

eval_cases.prompt: I want to make sure every single asset in my profile captures its custodian, broker, account or folio number, and login portal so I can easily locate and track them later. How does the FIRE Advisor support asset source tracking?
expected_criteria: Verifies that each asset entry contains explicit source metadata: custodian/broker platform, unique account/folio/ISIN/UAN/PRAN identifier, and portal URL
Generates an Asset Tracking & Source Ledger during profile evaluation aggregating all assets and liabilities
Validates source tracking across all categories (Cash/FDs, Equities/MFs, Pensions/EPF/SIPP, Gold/SGB, Real Estate, Crypto, Home Loans, and Term/Health Insurance)
Maintains complete local data privacy while providing an immediate audit trail for the client

eval_cases.capability: India AY 2026-27 Rebate, Marginal Relief & CTC Reconciliation
eval_cases.prompt: My annual CTC is ₹14 Lakhs. Does the new Indian tax regime make this tax-free? What is the difference between my CTC, gross salary, and taxable income under AY 2026-27 rules, and what happens if my taxable income slightly exceeds ₹12 Lakhs?
expected_criteria: Distinguishes CTC from Gross Taxable Salary and Net Taxable Income: explains that CTC includes employer EPF (12% of basic) and gratuity accrual (~4.81% of basic), which are not part of annual gross taxable pay

Explains that the official AY 2026-27 Section 87A rebate applies on Net Taxable Income up to ₹12,00,000 (after the ₹75,000 standard deduction, allowing up to ₹12.75L Gross Salary and ~₹13.5L-₹14L CTC with zero tax)
Calculates the exact Section 87A marginal relief formula for taxable income slightly exceeding ₹12 Lakhs, capping tax payable before cess to the income exceeding ₹12L
Demonstrates the versioned tax model supporting AY 2026-27 (default) and legacy AY 2025-26

eval_cases.capability: UK Scenario-Based Decumulation & Spousal Contribution Exceptions
eval_cases.prompt: With the April 2027 inheritance tax changes bringing pensions into the estate, should I always draw down my pension first? And my partner has no earned income—should we never fund their pension if we might retire into higher tax?
expected_criteria: Rejects unconditional 'Pensions First' rule: explains that optimal decumulation depends on estate size, Nil-Rate Bands (£325k-£1M), spousal exemption, current retiree tax rate, beneficiary tax rate, and GIA holdings

Identifies explicit exceptions where preserving pensions is superior: spousal beneficiaries (100% IHT exempt on first death), estates within nil-rate bands (0% IHT), and avoiding higher/60% marginal tax spikes during life

Rejects unconditional prohibition against non-earner pensions: demonstrates Personal Allowance Arbitrage yielding an immediate +25% return (£2,880 net -> £3,600 tax-free) when drawn within the £12,570 allowance
Highlights spousal pot equalization allowing the household to extract up to £25,140 tax-free annually across both Personal Allowances
